event.summary: Host-only fixture helpers do not strand supported old-terminal callers
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing the tmux branches from shared readiness, identity, exit and terminal-ending fixtures would break tests of sessions left by earlier releases. Details: harness.rs:1156-1185, 1204-1277, 1289-1349, 1714-1740 and 1819-1944 now require terminal hosts or end only hosts. The old-terminal fixture has its own server/guard and raw tmux access (old_terminals.rs:25-115); its shared wait_for_agent_ready call at :375 follows Restart and an explicit Host-row assertion at :367-374. Source-wide caller search at this revision found no shared readiness/end helper used to operate a still-tmux terminal. Exact governing contract, SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, Every new terminal in a host (:2236-2238): 'A supervisor creates every terminal in a terminal host; nothing selects tmux, and the supervisor never starts a tmux server'. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server (:2904-2906): 'The reload then takes every old-kind row as having no terminal, in any state, without looking its recorded pane id up'. The helper narrowing therefore follows the removed driver's replacement contract; no report proposed. Suggested bucket: other (test-tooling correctness if there were a route). Confidence: confirmed from source and contract, no runtime observation. proposed_drop: source refutation and quoted specification acceptance; the production supervisor no longer serves tmux terminals and the surviving migration caller uses a host after Restart. Could-be-highest: no; the considered consequence is fixture failure, with no established loss-of-work or security route. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: this is limited to the assigned fixture narrowing, not a review of the production retirement implementation.

event.summary: Optional trace boundary still isolates the guard's Drop evidence
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 303a1264b7bd791e8f6f6de2c7bb6136c08e8bab. TLDR: Considered whether removing the explicit diagnostic snapshot before teardown weakened the fixture test so it could pass on stale evidence. Details: harness/tmux_guard.rs:64-74 now independently asserts the owned session exists via has-session before dropping the guard. At :77-82 the boundary is None only when the assertion-safe capture contains no event; :115-139 then accepts all subsequent events in that empty case, or requires sequence greater than the last prior event. The capture preserves insertion order and assigns monotonically increasing sequence values under the collector lock (farhelm-testtrace/src/lib.rs:1363-1374, 1386-1414); snapshot/matching_events reject incomplete evidence (:598-628). Guard Drop collects and emits diagnostics before shutdown (farhelm-teststate/src/tmux/guard.rs:63-82). Therefore a previous iteration's events cannot satisfy the updated predicates; the first iteration no longer requires an unrelated earlier trace event. Contract: the supplied test-review checklist requires asserting the fixture premise before the action and an observable distinguishing the competing mechanisms. This test still asserts independent pre-Drop existence, post-boundary live-session diagnostics ordered before the shutdown event, and an independent post-Drop client failure. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutation; no stale-evidence route established. Could-be-highest: no; the considered effect is test coverage quality, without a catastrophic tooling or user-work route. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: existing reliance on a failing final list-sessions client as server absence is unchanged by this patch and is outside the new boundary logic.

event.summary: Moved drain helper bypasses grid transcript decoding
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: The shared terminal-draining fixture may mix encoded grid messages into the readable transcript that later test assertions inspect. Details: moved drain_for at harness.rs:2067-2089 directly extends seen with TermEvent::Data bytes, whereas append_transcript at :135-149 and wait_until at :2032-2034 decode grid data through grid_text. Callers retain the same seen buffer for later assertions/waits, e.g. session_lifecycle.rs:678-686 and tab_lifecycle_edges.rs:271-289. Checks made: read complete assigned patch, moved function, current callers and the grid transcript contract. The function is textually the same as its parent-revision implementation in terminal_backpressure.rs:20-43, so this may be an existing issue merely relocated. Exact missing premise: whether a current caller's assertion can materially be invalidated or falsely satisfied by the encoded payload, and whether the move changes exposure. Next source checks: inspect grid encoding and all drain consumers' assertions and parent caller mappings. Suggested bucket: other (test-tooling correctness). Confidence: unverified lead under active investigation, no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false pending source checks. Could-be-highest: no established route; only test transcript correctness is implicated. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: no finding claimed until source checks settle the consequence and change relevance.

event.summary: Raw grid bytes in moved drain do not establish a changed test failure
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: The drain helper appends encoded grid data to otherwise readable test transcripts, but the reviewed relocation does not establish an incorrect test outcome. Original suspected consequence preserved: a later assertion might falsely match or miss text because its buffer contains binary framing or non-screen messages. Details and checks: compared the full function against parent terminal_backpressure.rs:20-43; the implementation is unchanged. Compared all four consumer files across the commit: drain imports move into harness, while the drain calls and their assertions stay unchanged. Read all six call sites. Four calls use the drain result only to assert no detach and send their unique round-trip marker after the drain (session_lifecycle.rs:678-686 and :818-826, session_rename.rs:591-597, tab_lifecycle_edges.rs:271-289). The remaining two calls test absence of short plain text emitted by the other terminal (terminal_tabs.rs:1366-1393); GridOutput uses binary row encoding (farhelm-proto/src/grid.rs:1251-1282), whose write_row preserves each run's raw UTF-8 text (grid/binary.rs:120-152), and the fake basic agent's line uses one cyan style for its whole marker (fake_agent.rs:1715). No current late-drain assertion over decoded row joins, styles, or non-screen metadata was found. Contract: harness.rs:135-149 defines append_transcript as decoding grid data; using it would maintain a cleaner transcript invariant, but a cleanup opportunity without a demonstrated consequence is not a correctness finding. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed source observations and no established material consequence; no runtime observation. proposed_drop: unchanged relocation plus current caller analysis does not establish a failing or falsely passing assertion. Could-be-highest: no; the suspected effect remains test transcript correctness, not a security or user-work loss route. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: a future caller requiring decoded row concatenation must use append_transcript; no claim that this helper universally produces a valid text transcript. Lead settled as candidate; no missing source check remains for this initial pass.

event.summary: Removing tmux timeout floors does not shorten a surviving fixture budget
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether deleting the suite's generous tmux timeout floors reintroduced failures under machine load. Details: the assigned patch removes floor_suite_timeouts, suite_timeouts and suite_supervisor_with_timeouts and passes caller-supplied SupervisorTimeouts directly to the supervisor at harness.rs:1964-1972. Checked the full current SupervisorTimeouts definition at farhelm-supervisor/src/service/core.rs:362-436 and searched the supervisor source for tmux_exchange, tmux_pane_list and sink_ready: all three floored fields have been removed with their tmux consumers, so no remaining budget changes. Surviving stall, writer, upload, relay and host-end budgets are independent fields, which the old floor function left untouched. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server (:2887-2889), states 'The running supervisor runs no tmux at all, and its driver of the old terminals is gone'. Suggested bucket: other (test-tooling failures, if a route existed). Confidence: confirmed by source, not execution. proposed_drop: source refutation; the floored fields and operations no longer exist, and surviving caller overrides pass through unchanged. Could-be-highest: no; the considered consequence is test reliability without catastrophic tooling or user-work loss. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: no timing or load measurements were taken, and this does not assert the surviving host-specific budgets are sufficient under every machine load.
